chunks: Ḥasan ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Īsā narrated to me from Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Ḥanān ibn Sadīr, who said:

I was with Abī Ja’far (peace be upon him) when a man entered, said Salām to him, and sat down. Abū Ja’far (peace be upon him) asked him, 'From which lands are you?' The man said, 'I am a man from the people of Kūfah, and I am a lover of yours and a follower (muwālī).' Abū Ja’far (peace be upon him) asked him, 'Do you visit the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) every Friday?' He said, 'No.' He asked, 'What about every month?' He said, 'No.' He asked, 'What about every year?' He said, 'No.' Then Abū Ja’far (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Verily you are deprived of the good,' and he mentioned the hadith.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of visiting the grave of Imam al-Husain in Shia tradition according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Imam al-Baqir (a.s.) highlights the critical link between claimed love (mawala) and practical devotion by questioning a Kufan man’s neglect of visiting Husayn’s grave. The Imam’s declaration that he is 'deprived of good' underscores the Shia scholarly view that Ziyarah is not merely a ritual but a tangible proof of spiritual connection and fidelity to the Ahl al-Bayt.
